subject: ELECTRONICS
title: Verifying Ohm's law — resistance of a metallic wire
aim: Verify the linear relationship between potential difference V and current I across a constantan wire and find its resistance from the slope of V against I.

hazards.name: Wire heating
hazards.text: Open the key between readings so Joule heating does not raise the wire temperature and alter its resistance.

procedure: Assemble the series circuit (cells, key, rheostat, ammeter, and test wire) and connect the voltmeter in parallel across the wire.
Check both meters for zero error and choose ranges that avoid full-scale deflection.
Close the key, adjust the rheostat to set a clear current I, record both I and V, then open the key immediately.
Repeat for at least five well-spaced rheostat positions while keeping wire temperature near room temperature.
Plot potential difference V on the vertical axis against current I on the horizontal axis and compute the slope to find R.

precautions.text: Opened the key between readings to prevent the wire from heating up.
Checked and corrected for zero error on both the ammeter and voltmeter.
Ensured tight electrical connections and avoided parallax error when reading the analogue needles.

glossary.ohm's law: At constant temperature, the current through a metallic conductor is directly proportional to the potential difference across it.
glossary.rheostat: Variable resistor used to smoothly vary the current in a circuit.
glossary.zero error: Non-zero meter reading when no current or voltage is applied.
